extractions.value: On 6 April 1998 tightness of the left half of the face, difficulty moving the tongue, difficulty speaking and difficulty swallowing appeared and gradually worsened. From around early May stiffness of the leg muscles appeared, and both lower limbs would stiffen rapidly when touched. The left facial muscles of expression were constantly rigid, and the forehead wrinkles and nasolabial fold were more marked than on the right. The bilateral trapezius and sternocleidomastoid muscles were rigid, giving a hunched-shoulder posture. Rigidity of the trunk and upper limbs was not evident. The lower limbs were mildly rigid, left more than right, worsening with active and passive movement and becoming board-like; these findings disappeared during sleep.

extractions.value: Around 22 April, rapid involuntary movements of the face began to appear on tactile or painful stimulation. Somatosensory stimulation of the face or occiput, and auditory stimulation, produced myoclonus that retroflexed the neck and elevated both shoulders; no spreading movement to the upper or lower limbs was seen, and it was not evoked by tapping the trunk or the limbs. Somatosensory stimulation of the lower limbs produced myoclonus that rapidly stiffened both lower limbs; this was confined to the lower limbs and was not evoked by tapping the head and neck, trunk or upper limbs. Both types of myoclonus tended to weaken with repeated stimulation.

extractions.value: Clinical features (stiffness, reflex myoclonus), negative anti-GAD and anti-amphiphysin antibodies, surface EMG showing myoclonus with short burst discharges followed by tonic decrescendo activity, response to diazepam, and presence of mediastinal tumour suggesting paraneoplastic aetiology.
extractions.quote: These findings suggest that this stiff-man syndrome may occur as an autoimmune paraneoplastic syndrome of CNS.
A 58-year-old male presented with reflex myoclonus and stiffness of the left facial, tongue, shoulder, and lower limbs muscles.
No anti GAD antibody or anti amphiphysin antibody was detected in the serum and CSF.
On surface EMG the spasms initiated with 4–5 short burst discharges at intervals between 59 and 84 ms, followed by a tonic decrescendo activity up to 3 s.
After diazepam treatment, stiffness and reflex myoclonus of lower extrimiteties were disappeared and head retraction like reflex myoclonus was improved but remained.
CT of the chest revealed a mediastinal tumor.
No anti GAD antibody or anti amphiphysin antibody was detected in the serum and CSF.

Electrical cutaneous stimulation of the left dorsum of the foot produced a stiffening movement confined to both lower limbs. Surface EMG of the left quadriceps femoris, hamstrings, tibialis anterior and gastrocnemius showed reproducibility in the pattern of the myoclonus and of the sustained discharge: shortest latency 41 ms, followed by 5–6 nearly synchronous repeated contractions at intervals of 59–84 ms; from about 250 ms a sustained discharge appeared in all muscles and continued for several seconds while decrementing.

extractions.value: Patient received intramuscular tetanus toxoid injection at age 56. Tetanus antibody was very slightly raised at 0.31 IU/ml. Antinuclear antibody was speckled at ×160. Tumour marker NCC-ST-439 was raised at 28.6 U/ml, falling to 8.0 U/ml postoperatively. The number of repeated synchronous discharges differs between the Japanese abstract and English abstract (4–5) and the Japanese case-report text (5–6).
